comment: Raised from 7981 to 8195 for the scheduler fixes of pull request 12: each fix costs 4 to 35 B gzip, most of it try/catch on error paths. Raised from 8195 to 8216 for issue 10: a State written in a batch compares its value at the end with the value its readers saw. Raised from 8216 to 8517 for issue 11: mark, settle and stale walk a chain of memos with a list in place of recursion, and settle brings the sources of an out-of-date memo up to date first when reads are nested more than 100 deep, so a long chain does not overflow the stack on Melange. Lowered from 8517 to 8505 for issue 29: each keeps the first item of a duplicate key with one table of seen keys. Lowered from 8505 to 8502 for issue 29: Yuka re-exports State by alias, so Yuka.State is no object of its own. Raised from 8502 to 8524 for the runtime part of the static-hole drop: an effect or a hole whose first run reads no State is not kept by its owner, unless it adds a bubbling event handler. The server part (no markers for such a hole) was not kept: it cost 97 B more here and 0.23 MB more heap on /w/stress, for 30 fewer comment nodes on /insights. Raised from 8524 to 8583 for State.select: a read of a memo first updates a selector whose source changed (a list of pending selectors and its check in State.get and State.peek). Raised from 8583 to 8618 for the single yuka library: the bundle is 31 B smaller raw than on main (24226 against 24257 B), but Yuka.render now calls Client.render_root directly, and the swc mangler gives different short names across the bundle. Lower it when the app gets smaller.
